W.note: Exact 5-7-5 (Pearl-lit, high, unseen = 5; nacreous clouds bloom at dusk = 7; winter's rarest sky = 5) with an accurate nacreous/polar-stratospheric evocation, but "unseen" and "winter's rarest sky" are stock phrasing that tells the rarity instead of showing it.

X.note: Exact 5-7-5 (Late in autumn wind = 5; a lens above the ridge stands = 7; while the air runs through = 5) and a lenticular cloud that holds still while the wind passes through it, which is the real physics and a quietly strong turn.

Y.note: Shape is 4-7-4 (midwinter dusk = 4; a thin veil above the ridge = 7; turns pearl, then gray = 4), a deliberate tight short-long-short that makes the pearl-to-gray fading land, though the veil is less clearly identified as a specific cloud type.

Z.note: Exact 5-7-5 (Nacreous glow spreads = 5; across the winter dusk sky = 7; clouds no one expects = 5) with the correct nacreous name, but the imagery stays general and the closing "no one expects" turn is cute rather than earned.
